Challenges

What’s holding back your recovery from a Google penalty?

“My traffic dropped overnight, and I have no idea which update or penalty caused it.”

That is exactly where recovery starts. We match the drop against update timelines, Search Console data and your change history until the cause is proven, not guessed.

“I removed the spammy backlinks I knew about, but my rankings still haven’t recovered.”

Partial cleanups rarely lift a penalty. A full-profile audit usually finds the networks and patterns a quick pass misses — and documents every removal attempt properly.

“I submitted a reconsideration request months ago, and Google still hasn’t responded.”

Silence usually means the submission lacked evidence. We rebuild the case: complete cleanup logs, disavow file, and an honest account of what changed.

“My previous agency built the links that got us penalised, and now I don’t trust anyone with my site.”

A common story, and why everything we do is documented and visible to you — every link judged, every action logged, nothing hidden.

“I don’t know if this is a manual penalty or an algorithmic filter, and nobody can tell me clearly.”

The two need different remedies. Our forensic diagnosis separates them from data before a single change is made.

“My competitors do the same things and aren’t penalised. Why were we?”

Enforcement is uneven, but recovery is not a fairness argument — it is a cleanup standard. We bring the site fully inside the guidelines so the comparison stops mattering.

“I fixed the issues Google flagged, but rankings keep fluctuating instead of stabilising.”

Fluctuation after a fix usually means residual issues or an algorithmic case waiting on a refresh. We track weekly and keep cleaning until the line settles.

“I’m scared to make any more changes — the last changes made things worse.”

Understandable. Every change in a recovery is staged, reversible where possible, and explained before it happens. No surprises.

Our Process

Our Google penalty recovery process

1

Penalty identification & diagnosis

Manual action, algorithmic filter or not a penalty at all — established forensically from Search Console, update timelines and change history.

2

Thorough website audit

The full health check behind the diagnosis: technical, content and links, so nothing that contributed to the penalty is left standing.

3

Backlink analysis & cleanup

Every linking domain judged. Removal outreach first, then a disavow file built to Google’s standard for what cannot be removed.

4

Content optimisation

Thin, duplicated or manipulative content rebuilt to a genuine quality standard — or removed where it has no honest purpose.

5

Technical SEO fixes

Hacked pages, cloaking artefacts, structured-data abuse and other technical violations corrected and verified.

6

Reconsideration request submission

For manual actions: a complete, honest submission with the cleanup evidence reviewers need to say yes.

7

Monitoring & recovery tracking

Rankings and traffic tracked weekly through the recovery window, with the trend reported plainly — good or bad.

8

Preventative measures

Guideline-safe link and content practices replace whatever caused the penalty, with monitoring that catches risks early.

SEO Growth

Why penalty recovery must go further than fixing the violation

Not every drop is a penalty. Migrations, tracking errors and algorithm updates all mimic one. Our first job is forensic: match the drop against update timelines, Search Console messages and your change history to find the true cause.

If it is a penalty — toxic links, thin content, manipulative tactics from a previous provider — we clean it up properly, document everything, and file reconsideration requests that stand a real chance.

FAQs

FAQs on SEO penalty recovery services

How do I know if I have a penalty?

Check Search Console for manual actions first. Sudden drops aligned with known update dates suggest an algorithmic filter — our diagnosis confirms which.

How long does recovery take?

Manual actions can lift within weeks of a successful reconsideration. Algorithmic recovery usually needs a cleanup plus one or more update cycles — typically 3–6 months.

Can you guarantee recovery?

No one honestly can. We guarantee a correct diagnosis, a thorough cleanup and submissions that meet Google's stated standards.

Our previous agency built the bad links. Can you fix their work?

Yes — this is one of the most common reasons clients come to us. We audit everything they did and document the cleanup.

What is the difference between a manual action and an algorithmic penalty?

A manual action is applied by a human reviewer and appears in Search Console — it lifts when a reconsideration request succeeds. An algorithmic filter applies automatically; there is nothing to appeal, so recovery means cleaning up and being re-evaluated at the next refresh.

What happens if Google rejects our reconsideration request?

A rejection comes with clues about what remains. We work through them, extend the cleanup, document the additional work and resubmit — most of our successful recoveries were not first submissions.
